acceptanceClaims: two real successor processes observed the same exact dead-owner S6 ledger generation and exactly one acquired recovery authority while the loser remained non-mutating
the winning successor continued the admitted effect to peer-b-present and changed the durable ledger generation without changing semantic effect identity

after the winner was SIGKILLed, the losing successor re-read the newer ledger digest, acquired recovery authority against that exact current generation, and adopted the already-materialized effect without replay or physical mutation
the pre-fix overwrite-only current claim lost the first successor's recovery lineage even though physical mutual exclusion and retry were correct
the minimal fix archives exact predecessor claims and adds one-hop predecessorClaimId/predecessorClaimDigest to the new current claim without changing the kernel mutex
the final reconciler preserved the current successor claim and archived predecessor claim in its receipt before closing the world and deleting recovery metadata
persistent peer-B topology remained valid even after the one-shot challenge service naturally exited, separating persistent consequence from transient service liveness
limitations: the physical experiment uses one Linux Host and does not prove distributed successor ownership or fencing
winner selection and fairness are intentionally unspecified
only two successor candidates were physically tested
successor death during the continuation suffix itself remains untested
generic exactly-once semantics, shared-resource concurrency and causal-DAG requirements remain unproved
the accepted Range remains structurally unrouted and does not authorize external or uncontrolled targets
